ll_kilburn_milton.summary: A 1905 Winnebago County history identifies an exact-name Milton Kilburn as coming from New Hampshire to the Rockford area in 1835 and later serving as the county's first probate judge. The exact name, year and northern-Illinois geography make this a plausible lead for the Chicago post-office entry, but no source yet ties this man to Chicago or the letter itself, so the identification is not asserted.

candidates.name: Milton Kilburn, early Rockford/Winnebago County settler
candidates.basis: Exact name; reported arrival in northern Illinois in 1835.
conflicts: The source places him in the Rockford area rather than Chicago and provides no postal, address, kinship or occupation discriminator tying him to the Chicago letter-list entry.

ll_jesse_hobson.summary: A retrospective Hobson genealogy places an exact-name Jesse Hobson in the Naperville/Chicago area from about 1830 and records his marriage to Catherine Daugherty on 6 April 1835. That Cook-area chronology is close to the 20 May 1835 Chicago letter-list return and is a strong identity lead, but the genealogy is retrospective and does not itself connect the man to the postal entry, so no household fact is promoted.

candidates.name: Jesse Hobson (1812-1883), Naperville-area settler
candidates.basis: Exact uncommon name; near-Chicago residence before 1835; dated April 1835 marriage in the same regional context as the May Chicago post-office return.
conflicts: The reviewed source is a later genealogy rather than a contemporary record and does not explicitly state that he received or awaited mail at Chicago.
